meta.title: GitOps with Argo CD
meta.eyebrow: Hands-on path, from the first cluster to a full pipeline
meta.subtitle: Install, sync, scale to many environments and deliver safely
meta.description: A roadmap to learn GitOps in practice with Argo CD and Kubernetes, in seven weeks.
meta.tagline:
Git as the source of truth.
A local cluster to break things on.
meta.sidebarNote:
Break things on a practice cluster.
Every mistake shows how Argo CD reacts.

phases.title: Fundamentals
phases.summary: Understand GitOps, set up a practice cluster and sync a first application.

phases.title: Operations
phases.summary: Control how and when Argo CD applies changes.

phases.title: Scale
phases.summary: Many environments, many teams, and secrets out of plain text.

phases.title: Progressive delivery
phases.summary: Connect continuous integration to the repository and release with less risk.

nodes.title: GitOps on one page
nodes.summary: The core idea: the desired state lives in Git and a controller in the cluster makes reality match it.
topics: Git as the source of truth
nodes.challenge: Write a paragraph explaining the difference between a CI script deploy and a GitOps deploy.
nodes.success: You explain why nobody needs cluster access any more to ship a release.

nodes.title: A local practice cluster
nodes.summary: A disposable cluster on your computer, to create and destroy without fear.
nodes.challenge: Create a cluster, list the nodes and remove the cluster completely.
nodes.success: You recreate the cluster from scratch in a few minutes.

tasks.title: Install kubectl and kind
Create the practice cluster
List the nodes with kubectl get nodes
Create a test namespace

nodes.title: Install Argo CD
nodes.summary: Put Argo CD in the cluster and reach the web interface and the command line.
nodes.challenge: Open the web interface with the initial password and also log in through the CLI.
nodes.success: You can explain what each installed component does.

tasks.title: Create the argocd namespace
Apply the install manifests
Open the interface with a port forward
Get the initial admin password
tasks.note: It is in a Secret created during the install.

tasks.title: Install the CLI and log in

nodes.title: Your first Application
nodes.summary: Point Argo CD at a repository of manifests and watch the application appear in the cluster.
nodes.challenge: Publish a simple deployment through a Git repository, then change the replica count through Git.
nodes.success: A change in the repository shows up in the cluster after a sync.

tasks.title: Create the repository with the manifests
Create the Application in the interface
Recreate the same Application in YAML
Sync and check the resources
Change something in the cluster and see OutOfSync
tasks.note: This is the drift Argo CD detects.

nodes.title: Automatic sync
nodes.summary: Let Argo CD apply on its own and decide what to do with what vanished from Git or was changed by hand.
nodes.challenge: Turn on auto sync with self heal, delete a resource by hand and watch Argo CD recreate it.
nodes.success: You know when prune and self heal are useful and when they can surprise you.

nodes.title: Sync notifications
nodes.summary: Tell a chat channel when a deploy finishes or fails.

nodes.title: Helm and Kustomize
nodes.summary: Reuse manifests with per environment values instead of copying files.
nodes.challenge: Publish the same application in two namespaces with different values.
nodes.success: The two environments differ only in a values file or an overlay.

tasks.title: Publish a Helm chart through Argo CD
Split the values per environment
Redo the same thing with Kustomize

nodes.title: Helm charts
nodes.summary: Package the application as a chart and publish it through an Argo CD Application.

nodes.title: Values per environment
nodes.summary: One values file per environment, kept next to the Application that uses it.

nodes.title: Kustomize overlays
nodes.summary: A shared base plus one overlay per environment.

nodes.title: Jsonnet
nodes.summary: Only worth it if your team already writes Jsonnet.

nodes.title: Sync waves and hooks
nodes.summary: Control the order in which resources are applied and run tasks before or after the deploy.
nodes.challenge: Run a migration job before starting the deployment, using an earlier wave.
nodes.success: The deployment only starts after the job finishes successfully.

nodes.title: ApplicationSet
nodes.summary: Generate many Applications from one template, one per environment, cluster or folder.
nodes.challenge: Generate one Application per environment folder from a single ApplicationSet.
nodes.success: Creating a new folder in Git creates a new application, without editing Argo CD.

nodes.title: Many clusters
nodes.summary: Register extra clusters and publish to them from the same Argo CD.

nodes.title: Projects and RBAC
nodes.summary: Separate teams and environments: who can publish what, and to which cluster.
nodes.challenge: Create a project that can only publish to one namespace and test an attempt outside it.
nodes.success: An attempt to publish outside the project is refused with a clear message.

nodes.title: Secrets in GitOps
nodes.summary: Plain text secrets in Git are a bad idea. There are ways to version them without exposing them.
nodes.challenge: Deliver a secret to the cluster without its value appearing in plain text in the repository.
nodes.success: You explain what stays in Git and what stays out of it.

nodes.title: CI that updates Git
nodes.summary: Continuous integration builds the image and writes the new version to the manifest repository. Argo CD does the rest.
nodes.challenge: A commit to the code produces a new image and a commit to the manifest repository.
nodes.success: The deploy happens with no manual command on the cluster.

tasks.title: Build and publish the image in CI
Update the tag in the manifest repository
Require review for the production environment

nodes.title: Canary delivery
nodes.summary: Release a version to part of the traffic and move forward only if everything is healthy.
nodes.challenge: Make a faulty version get stopped and rolled back on its own.
nodes.success: A bad version never reaches all users.

nodes.title: Production checklist
nodes.summary: What to review before you truly depend on Argo CD.
nodes.challenge: A short list of what is missing for Argo CD to be the only way into production.
nodes.success: You know what happens to deploys if Argo CD becomes unavailable.

projects.title: Your app, synced from Git
projects.summary: Put a small app in a Git repository and let Argo CD deploy it.

requirements.title: A repository with the manifests of a small web app
An Application that points to that repository
Change the number of replicas with a commit and watch it sync
A README explaining how to reproduce it

projects.deliverable: A public repository with the manifests, the Application and the README.
projects.success: Someone with a local cluster can follow the README and see the app running.
stretch: Expose the app with an Ingress

projects.title: Self-healing demo
projects.summary: Show that the cluster goes back to what Git says, even after manual changes.

requirements.title: Turn on automatic sync with prune and self-heal
Delete a Deployment and edit a Service by hand
Record or screenshot Argo CD fixing both
Explain in the README what each setting did

projects.deliverable: A short write-up with the screenshots or a recording.
projects.success: Every manual change goes back to the Git version without anyone touching it.
stretch: Use a sync window to block syncs at night

projects.title: One app, three environments
projects.summary: Run the same app in dev, staging and prod, promoted by pull request.

requirements.title: dev, staging and prod with Kustomize overlays or Helm values
Different replicas, resources and config per environment
A database migration as a PreSync hook
Promoting a version is a pull request that changes one file

projects.deliverable: A repository with the three environments and a README of the promotion flow.
projects.success: A new version reaches prod only through merged pull requests, and the migration runs before the app.
stretch: Add a smoke test as a PostSync hook

projects.title: A small platform for teams
projects.summary: Let several teams deploy their apps safely from one repository.

requirements.title: An ApplicationSet that creates one app per folder
One AppProject per team, limited to its namespaces
Roles so each team syncs only its own apps
Adding a team is creating a folder and a pull request

projects.deliverable: A repository with the ApplicationSet, the projects and an onboarding guide.
projects.success: A team cannot deploy outside its namespaces, and a new team is live after one merge.

projects.title: From commit to canary
projects.summary: A complete delivery flow: CI builds, Git records, Argo CD deploys with a canary.

requirements.title: CI builds the image and updates the tag in the config repository
Secrets stored encrypted in Git (Sealed Secrets or SOPS)
A canary release with Argo Rollouts
Automatic rollback when an analysis fails
A diagram of the whole flow in the README

projects.deliverable: Two repositories (app and config) and a recording of a failed canary rolling back.
projects.success: A bad version is stopped and rolled back without anyone stepping in.
stretch: Notifications for each step in a chat channel

projects.title: Production readiness review
projects.summary: Take an Argo CD setup through a production checklist and prove it.

requirements.title: Argo CD in high availability mode
Metrics and alerts for Argo CD itself
A backup of the Argo CD config, restored in a new cluster
SSO or local users with least privilege
A runbook for when Argo CD is down

projects.deliverable: The checklist with evidence for each item, and the runbook.
projects.success: You restore the whole setup in an empty cluster by following only the runbook.
stretch: Run a game day with a teammate breaking things
